original_question: Classify rigid non-invertible dominant holomorphic germs in complex dimension 3.
target_in_paper: Open Problem (OP11) in §3.3, “Non-invertible systems: rigidification”: “Classify 3-dimensional non-invertible dominant rigid germs.” ([pagine.dm.unipi.it](https://pagine.dm.unipi.it/abate/articoli/artric/files/10.1007_s13324-011-0017-y.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper’s actual target very closely: it names the right object class (rigid, non-invertible, dominant holomorphic germs) and the right dimension (3), which is essentially the wording of OP11. ([pagine.dm.unipi.it](https://pagine.dm.unipi.it/abate/articoli/artric/files/10.1007_s13324-011-0017-y.pdf))
missing_details: The paper’s notion of “classification” is the general one introduced in the introduction: finding normal forms under local holomorphic conjugacy. OP11 itself does not restate that, so a stand-alone version should make the equivalence relation explicit. ([pagine.dm.unipi.it](https://pagine.dm.unipi.it/abate/articoli/artric/files/10.1007_s13324-011-0017-y.pdf))

The ambient objects are holomorphic fixed-point germs f:(M,p)->(M,p); by local coordinates, one may equivalently work with germs in End(C^3,O). The draft does not state this ambient setting. ([pagine.dm.unipi.it](https://pagine.dm.unipi.it/abate/articoli/artric/files/10.1007_s13324-011-0017-y.pdf))

The draft does not define “non-invertible”; in the paper this means that df_p is not invertible, equivalently that 0 is an eigenvalue of df_p. ([pagine.dm.unipi.it](https://pagine.dm.unipi.it/abate/articoli/artric/files/10.1007_s13324-011-0017-y.pdf))

The draft does not define “dominant”; in the paper’s several-variable notation this means det Jac(f) is not identically zero. ([pagine.dm.unipi.it](https://pagine.dm.unipi.it/abate/articoli/artric/files/10.1007_s13324-011-0017-y.pdf))

The draft does not define “rigid.” To make the question stand-alone, one should specify Crit(f)={det(df)=0}, Crit∞(f)=union_{k>=0} f^{-k}(Crit(f))=union_{k>=0} Crit(f^k), and require that, as a germ at the fixed point, Crit∞(f) has q smooth irreducible components W_1,...,W_q with 0<=q<=3 having simple normal crossings, and that for each j there exists I_j subset {1,...,q} such that f(W_j)=intersection_{i in I_j} W_i. ([pagine.dm.unipi.it](https://pagine.dm.unipi.it/abate/articoli/artric/files/10.1007_s13324-011-0017-y.pdf))
refined_question: Classify, up to local holomorphic conjugacy, the 3-dimensional non-invertible dominant rigid holomorphic fixed-point germs f:(M,p)->(M,p) over C (equivalently, after choosing local coordinates, germs f in End(C^3,O)) such that df_p is not invertible, det Jac(f) is not identically zero, and the generalized critical set Crit∞(f):=union_{k>=0} f^{-k}(Crit(f))=union_{k>=0} Crit(f^k), where Crit(f)={det(df)=0}, is, as a germ at p, the union of q smooth irreducible components W_1,...,W_q with 0<=q<=3 having simple normal crossings at p and satisfying f(W_j)=intersection_{i in I_j} W_i for some I_j subset {1,...,q} for each j. ([pagine.dm.unipi.it](https://pagine.dm.unipi.it/abate/articoli/artric/files/10.1007_s13324-011-0017-y.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, because any holomorphic local dynamical system at a point of a 3-dimensional complex manifold is locally holomorphically conjugate to one at O in C^3, classify up to local holomorphic conjugacy the germs f in End(C^3,O) satisfying the same non-invertible, dominant, and rigid conditions. ([pagine.dm.unipi.it](https://pagine.dm.unipi.it/abate/articoli/artric/files/10.1007_s13324-011-0017-y.pdf))
justification: The draft is targeting OP11, not OP12: it asks for the classification of rigid germs themselves, whereas OP12 asks when a general germ in End(C^3,O) admits a rigidification after modification. The nearby context in §3.3 supplies the hidden definition of rigidity via Crit∞(f), and Theorem 12 explains why this classification problem is the right three-dimensional analogue of the known dimension-2 story: every non-invertible dominant germ in End(C^2,O) is birationally conjugated to a rigid germ, and the text immediately notes that the 2-dimensional classification of rigid germs gives birational normal forms. The introduction’s general discussion of classification problems supports making the intended equivalence relation explicit as local holomorphic conjugacy. ([pagine.dm.unipi.it](https://pagine.dm.unipi.it/abate/articoli/artric/files/10.1007_s13324-011-0017-y.pdf))
